what: the feature-maturity point table, version 1. Every entry is points a thing earns for a quality it verifiably has. There are no denominators and no ceilings: a percentage moves when the thing it divides by moves, which makes it useless as a build gate, so percentages survive in this lane only as diagnostics. More good data is more score, and nothing is ever done.
monotonicity: a build is compared to the build before it under the same table version. A re-weighting is a new version, not a mass failure, and builds under different versions are simply not compared. A decrease is permitted only where the ledger carries corrections that account for it.

featureNotes.name: a feature that is called something.
featureNotes.prose: a feature that is explained in writing at all.
featureNotes.proseSubstance: a second point once the prose is longer than substanceChars, which is where a description stops being a longer label and starts being an explanation.
featureNotes.geo: true planetary coordinates, both axes, as the source published them.
featureNotes.membership: one point per membership attribute the feature carries -- which subwatershed its ground lies in, and whatever joins come after.
featureNotes.icon: the collection it belongs to resolves artwork, so the feature is drawn as something rather than as a dot.
featureNotes.geometryLog: points per doubling of vertices: floor(log2(1+vertices)) times this. Ground that is actually drawn is worth more than ground that is claimed, and log scaling means a detailed boundary beats a rectangle without letting one over-noded polygon outweigh a city.
featureNotes.corroboration: one point per other reading that pinned this same place, read off the merge ledger. Two sources agreeing is evidence, and evidence is quality.

collectionNotes.convention: one point per registered semantic-conventions key the collection declares. A collection that says how it renders, what kind it is, and what its stroke weight means is machine-readable in a way one that says nothing is not.

worldNotes.convention: one point per registered world-level key: what surface this is, how it was flattened, what body it pictures, how big that body is.
worldNotes.lens: one point per picture of the ground.
worldNotes.lensZoom: one point per zoom level a picture actually holds, which is the honest measure of how much raster detail a reader can get to.
